summary: Summit station on Mount Hood from 1915: a firefinder, then a D-6 cupola cabin; abandoned 1935 and slipped off the summit in 1941. No source read describes the summit today.

facts.design: Firefinder and tent on the summit cairn (1915), replaced later that year by a Lige Coleman prototype for the D-6 cupola cabin
facts.status_note: Cabin abandoned in 1935 and slipped off the summit in 1941; no source we read describes the summit site today
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Hood National Forest

events.note: Firefinder and tent on the summit cairn, replaced later that year by a Lige Coleman prototype for the D-6 cupola cabin
Lige Coleman (also Coalman) put in charge of the summit station
Mark Weygandt succeeded Coalman as observer by late September 1918
Register and firelookout.com say the cabin was abandoned in 1935

evidence.supports: 1915 seasonal fire lookout stationed at the summit
evidence.quote: In the summer of 1915, the U.S. Forest Service launched a bold experiment: a seasonal fire lookout stationed at the summit of Mount Hood.

evidence.supports: July 1915 plan to survey the Bull Run forest reserve year round
evidence.quote: July 21, 1915: From the frigid peak of Mount Hood a lookout is to survey the Bull Run forest reserve the year around

evidence.supports: 1915 firefinder and tent on the summit cairn
evidence.quote: The USFS constructed a firefinder on top of the summit cairn and a tent with a wooden floor in 1915.

evidence.supports: tent replaced later in 1915 by a Lige Coleman prototype for the D-6 cupola cabin
evidence.quote: This was replaced later the same year by a Lige Coleman prototype for the D-6 cupola cabin.

evidence.supports: Lige Coleman in charge of the station (1915)
evidence.quote: Lige Coleman will be in charge of the station.

evidence.supports: Coalman spelling and succession by Weygandt
evidence.quote: September 28, 1918: A landslide moving an enormous mass of ice and stone down the northeast side of Mount Hood was recently witnessed by Mark Weygandt, who succeeded Elijah Coalman as observer at the forestry lookout station.

evidence.supports: August 3, 1918 Oregonian: Coalman had resigned recently
evidence.quote: August 3, 1918: Elijah Coalman, who for many years has been in the lookout station at Government camp and who resigned recently

evidence.supports: abandoned 1935; cabin slipped off the summit 1941
evidence.quote: Abandoned in 1935, the cabin slipped off the summit in 1941.

evidence.supports: U.S. Forest Service administers the site

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Coalman in Forest Lookouts and the 1918 Oregonian item; Coleman in the register, firelookout.com and the 1915 Journal quote. The story uses Coalman and notes Coleman.

notes_for_editor: Record height_m 68.6 (225 ft) is not supported by any source read; the sources describe a summit cupola cabin and give no height, so facts omit it and no correction is proposed. The record's kind 'ground' is not contradicted, but no source says ground-mounted; check. Elevation 3427.5 m matches firelookout.com's 11,245 ft. Sources read agree on 1935 abandonment and 1941 collapse. A web search summary mentioned other abandonment years and remains on the summit; those pages were not opened, so they are not cited or used. Budget: 1 search, 6 page reads.
